record.paper_title: Open problems on regular languages: an historical perspective
record.context_brief: Existence of regular languages of star-height 2
record.original_question: An extended rational expression is built from letters using Boolean operations, concatenation, and the Kleene star, and the star-height of such an expression is the maximum nesting depth of star operations. The star-height of a regular language is the minimum star-height among all extended rational expressions defining it. Does there exist any regular language whose star-height is exactly 2, meaning that every defining extended rational expression requires nesting the star operation to depth at least 2?

evidence.quote:
The star-height of such an expression
is the maximum number of nested stars occurring in the expression.
The star-height of a language is the minimal star-height of an expression representing the language.

However, it is an open problem to know whether there are languages of
star-height 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a finite alphabet A. The class of extended rational (regular) expressions over A is defined inductively: every letter a ∈ A, the empty word, and the empty set are extended rational expressions; and if E and F are extended rational expressions, then so are the Boolean combinations E ∪ F, E ∩ F, and the complement Eᶜ (with respect to A*), the concatenation E·F, and the Kleene star E*. The star-height h(E) of an extended rational expression E is defined by: h(a) = h(∅) = h(ε) = 0; h(E ∪ F) = h(E ∩ F) = h(E·F) = max(h(E), h(F)); h(Eᶜ) = h(E); and h(E*) = h(E) + 1. The (generalized) star-height of a regular language L ⊆ A* is the minimum of h(E) over all extended rational expressions E that denote L.

Question: Does there exist a regular language L over some finite alphabet whose generalized star-height equals 2; equivalently, is there a regular language that cannot be denoted by any extended rational expression in which the Kleene star is nested to depth at most 1?
artifact.status_search_result: The generalized star-height problem remains open. It is unknown whether any regular language has generalized star-height greater than 1; in particular, no regular language has been proven to have star-height exactly 2. Wikipedia and J.-E. Pin's problem page confirm the problem's open status.

status_evidence.title: Generalized star-height problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is unknown whether or not there exists a language of generalized star height greater than 1.
status_evidence.claim: No regular language is known to require generalized star-height > 1.

status_evidence.title: The star-height problem (J.-E. Pin)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem page maintained listing the generalized star-height problem as open.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is still listed as open.
